summary: Washington light and fog signal at the turn from the Strait of Juan de Fuca into Admiralty Inlet, lit 1879; the 1914 octagonal tower is leased to the U.S. Lighthouse Society.

access.note: Coast Guard property leased to the U.S. Lighthouse Society since 2019; lighthouse closed to the public; visible from the beach at Fort Worden State Park.

stay.note: Society rents the 1879 keepers duplex and the Coast Guard house (per Point Wilson Light Station website).

notes_for_editor: Thin primary base for the first half-century: the corpus holds Light-House Board reports only from 1891, so 1879-1890 construction details (funding dates, contractor, lens from Point Bonita), the 1886 fence and the 1896 Umatilla grounding rest on LighthouseFriends alone; newspaper searches on Chronicling America were too slow to complete. Disagreements: Littlefield left 1883 (USLHS) or 1884 (HistoryLink); range 13 miles (HistoryLink, LF) or nine (Keeper's Log); Governor deaths nine (Bulletin, Commissioner) or eight (HistoryLink, NRHP, LF); church bell donor Sheldon (LF) or Seldon (HistoryLink); fog signal in 1914 chime diaphone (HistoryLink) vs siren with horn in fiscal 1917 (Commissioner). The 1894 report entry matched by scan page; the print page is read as p.195 but unconfirmed. Roster lines are the USLHS archive as printed (88 lines); Coast Guard-era names are as the archive prints them. 1915 flag list matched by table position (17th District). USLHS lists Score from 1895, LF from 1894 (acting 1894-95 per archive). Fog-signal hour counts come from OCR text. The record says range 15 nm and focal height 15.5 m; not rechecked. Access in the record says public; the sources say the lighthouse is closed (grounds are on Coast Guard/Society property).
